title: n8n attributes an execution to a workflow, never to the human who decided
content:
`execution_entity` carries `id`, `status`, `mode`, `createdAt`, `startedAt` and a `DeleteDateColumn` for soft deletion. `mode` is an enum over how the run was triggered: `webhook`, `trigger`, `manual`, `cli`, `retry`. The payload sits in `execution_data` as a single `text` blob, cascade-deleted with its parent row.

Nowhere in either entity is there a field for the deciding actor, the rule applied, or the prior state. An execution is attributed to a *workflow* — to the automation that ran, not to the person on whose authority it ran.

This is the structural reason an n8n execution log cannot answer "who approved this, under which rule", independently of retention. Even a run preserved forever would not carry the attribution.
description: The mode field is an enum of trigger types — webhook, trigger, manual, cli, retry — so there is no field recording which person made the decision under which rule.
